learning: If s-bend and slalom still reach max_error 0.06 at base_speed 1.3, the limit is gain or sensing reach, not speed. If oscillation stays high, the next lever is kd or mass, not kp.
notes: Geometry held at iteration 1 values, as the Builder requested. Controller changed to base_speed 1.3, kp 2.4 and kd 0.5 to reduce bend drift and damp the oscillation that higher gain would add.
rationale: Iteration 1 moved the sensors to y = 0.06 m and raised kp from 1.2 to 2.0 (kd 0.3). Compared with iteration 0, the oval now finishes 4 of 20 trials and mean score rose from 50.7 to 166.4. The s-bend (progress 0.206) and slalom (progress 0.136) still leave the track at max_error of about 0.060 to 0.062 m. Line-loss events stay low (0.85, 1.0 and 2.0), so the sensors still see the tape and the failure is drift, not lost sensing. Oscillation on the oval rose from 0.07 to 0.18, so more kp alone risks instability. I therefore keep the geometry unchanged, as the Builder asked, and change only the controller in two ways. I lower base_speed from 1.6 to 1.3, since the drift on the tighter bends suggests the robot is entering them too fast to correct. Oval mean finish time was 1.885 s at 1.6, so about 2.3 s at 1.3 still fits the 3 s limit. I also raise kd from 0.3 to 0.5 to damp the oscillation that a higher kp would bring, and raise kp from 2.0 to 2.4 for more correction per unit of signal. ki stays at 0 and line_loss stays last_direction, since line losses are low and the sign convention is verified. Expected, not measured: fewer off-track ends on the s-bend and slalom, with progress above 0.2, and oval completion holding. The main risk is that kd 0.5 with the 60 mm look-ahead causes jitter on the sharpest bend.
